findings.reason: the node's principal equality check is written against a key that no committed receipt carries, so a worker either fails to resolve the referent or reads the wrong file whose existence the plan never requires.
findings.text: done-when (1) names the referent for its equality as "the fitted equivalent ampere-turns (`equivalent_current_a_turn`) in that frame's `correction-<frame>.json` receipt", but that receipt is written by `scripts/prototypes/diiid_xpoint_coil_correction/fit.py:81-82` as `json.dumps(correction)` — a bare conductor-name-to-amperes mapping — so the key `equivalent_current_a_turn` is absent from it; the name exists only in the in-memory attribution result (`scripts/prototypes/diiid_xpoint_attribution/attribute.py:102`, asserted in `tests/test_xpoint_attribution.py:91`), and the sibling file `conductor-fit-<frame>.json` holds the same numbers under `equivalent_error_a_turn`, a field the plan does not name

response_events.note: The equality now reads the conductor-name mapping that fit.py writes to correction-<frame>.json, and names equivalent_error_a_turn in conductor-fit-<frame>.json as the same values.
